llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly retrieves NetIncome.xlsx from the environment and extracts all needed state: Sheet2 column A header and row count, Sheet1 column C header, row count, and sum.

Metric covers all 4 sub-goals from the scoring breakdown: (1) Sheet2 Revenue header+19 rows (0.4), (2) Sheet1 C1 Net Income header case-insensitive (0.2), (3) Sheet1 column C 19 data rows (0.2), (4) Net Income sum == 456100 (0.2).
Negative control resistance is solid: initial file has no Sheet2 and no column C, so the evaluator will correctly score 0.0 on the unmodified file.
Using openpyxl with data_only=True is the correct approach for reading formula-computed values cached in a saved xlsx file.
Sum check (abs difference < 1) is a strong proxy for per-row correctness of Revenue - Total Expenses calculation given the pre-computed expected value of 456100.
Partial credit structure (0.4 + 0.2 + 0.2 + 0.2) appropriately rewards partial completion of this chained multi-goal task.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Consider verifying that Sheet2 row count scan matches the actual data range in the source file (rows 2-20 = 19 rows) to guard against edge cases where data might extend beyond row 20.
